My arms feel heavy and numb, my chest burns, and I can hear my own panicked breathing echoing with its low, laughing growl as its hollow eyes lock on mine. Their eyes flutter open just enough to look at me, terrified, and their mouth moves like they’re trying to say something, but all that comes out is a wet, choking sound that I can feel in my bones. I try to press my hands over the wound, but the blood keeps pushing through my fingers, hotter and faster, and I realize they’re going still while I’m screaming for help into the empty, silent street.

contexts: I’m standing alone in a dim bathroom, the fluorescent light above me buzzing and flickering, and when I look into the mirror, my reflection seems a second too slow, like it’s hesitating. Then I see my face starting to sag and slide downward in the glass—my skin glossy and wet, peeling off in thick, melting folds like wax—and I can hear a soft dripping hitting the sink even though I’m too terrified to move. I grab my cheeks and they feel hot, loose, and slippery under my fingers, and when I try to scream, my mouth stretches wrong, the skin around it collapsing as my own distorted reflection stares back at me with eyes that are sinking lower and lower. I’m frozen there, watching my face pour off my skull in the mirror while the dripping gets louder, and just as my reflection opens its melting mouth like it’s about to say something, the lights cut out.
